verdict.rationale: New Relic documents NRQL, a SQL-like language for querying its data, and a logs UI that lets you filter down by text or other attributes. Nothing in the pack says arbitrary high-cardinality fields such as user or request IDs can be grouped ad hoc without pre-aggregation or index setup. One community report describes metric-name explosions from unique URLs that ended with metric creation being locked, a cardinality limit on metrics specifically. missing for 10: explicit documentation of grouping (e.g., FACET) on high-cardinality attributes, a statement that no indexes or pre-aggregation are needed, independent hands-on corroboration at high cardinality.

support.subject: As a developer, I can group and filter by high-cardinality fields (user id, request id) without pre-aggregating or defining indexes first

citations.quote: New Relic Query Language (NRQL) is a SQL-like language for querying your New Relic data.
From the main logs UI page, you can see all your logs and then filter down to logs with specific text, or other attributes.
